One-off structural observation on 2026-11-18 against test.oblak.host on cPanel 11.138.0.24, using the generic call() at master 8c2834de on the disposable account wldnszed, which the run created and removed (absence confirmed afterwards). Every request was a form POST, sent once through direct UAPI and once through the WHM bridge. Only value types and upstream error text were recorded; no payload was stored. mass_edit_zone on both routes: two repeated add fields both created their TXT records; one call with an edit and a remove, using line_index values from parse_zone, changed exactly those records; both successes returned data.new_serial as a JSON string of digits. A call with no change, a stale serial, malformed add JSON and a zone the account does not control each returned status 0 with the zone unchanged. The stale-serial failure returned data with a string type and a null detail; the others returned null data. The malformed-JSON error text quoted the supplied add text. Source read on the same server (Cpanel/API/DNS.pm, Cpanel/Admin/Modules/Cpanel/zone.pm): the function needs one of the simplezoneedit, zoneedit or changemx features, refuses demo mode, reads add, edit and remove with get_length_multiple and authorizes every record_type against the types the account features allow.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 96. Updates one of the account's DNS zones in one form POST with no rollback. Temporary domains are unsupported. The supplied SOA serial must match the zone's current serial or the request fails. The documented serial and removal-index minima are zero; the client adds no range check.

Both remove indexes and edit line_index are 0-based zone-file line indexes: use line_index from parseZone(). add and edit items are caller-serialized JSON objects with dname, ttl, record_type and data; edit also needs line_index. The number and format of the data strings depend on record_type. The strings are forwarded unchanged, including malformed text.

Each supplied family must be a nonempty sequential list: strict strings for add and edit, integers for remove. Items become repeated literal add, edit and remove fields in caller order, keeping duplicates and exact bytes, with no parsing or index conversion. Null omits a family. Omitting all three still sends serial and zone; the client adds no minimum-one-change rule.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24, through direct UAPI and the WHM bridge, new_serial arrived as a string of digits; it is returned as an integer. Two repeated add fields both landed, and an edit plus a removal by parseZone() line_index changed exactly those records.

On the same server a call without changes, a stale serial, malformed add JSON and a zone the account does not control each failed with ApiErrorException and no zone change. The stale-serial failure carries a data object that the exception does not expose. The malformed-JSON error text quotes the supplied record text, so errors() can contain record data: treat it as private.

Source read on cPanel 11.138.0.24: the function needs one of the simplezoneedit, zoneedit or changemx features and is refused in demo mode. The record types it accepts depend on those features; a record_type outside them fails the whole call. No record-type enum is enforced locally.

The pinned text says each surviving record keeps its line count, not that line offsets stay unchanged: read the zone again before reusing indexes. The client makes one request with no reread, serial refresh, retry or rollback, and promises no DNS propagation. A PayloadMismatchException after a successful envelope follows a zone that already changed; do not retry it.

Whostmgr/DNS/SwapIP.pm replaces A records whose address is a source address, gives names that start with ftp. the FTP address, rewrites every SPF TXT record, detects a missing source address once for the whole batch, and increases the serial of, synchronizes and reloads every processed zone.

notes.text: Available from cPanel 96. Replaces an IPv4 address in the DNS zones of the given domains with destIp, with no rollback. Without sourceIp the server detects the address to replace: the zone root's A record, otherwise the first A record that is not a loopback address. Without ftpIp, FTP records receive destIp.

A scalar domain sends one domain field. A nonempty sequential string list, including a list of one, repeats the literal domain field in caller order. The pinned text also describes numbered names but disagrees with its own example about the first index, so this method never numbers. Domains and addresses are forwarded unchanged; the client validates neither.

On cPanel 11.138.0.24 direct UAPI returned rows with all five string fields for one domain and for a repeated domain list. Through the WHM bridge every call that reached the zone update failed with ApiErrorException (Undefined subroutine &Cpanel::AdminBin::Call::call): the handler calls the admin layer without loading it. Input errors still reported normally on both routes. The client keeps the bridge route and adds no fallback; this is one build, not every version.

Source read on cPanel 11.138.0.24: A records whose address equals a source address are replaced, and names starting with ftp. receive the FTP address. Every SPF TXT record is rewritten and reported whether or not an address matched, and each processed zone gets a new serial and is synchronized and reloaded. A sourceIp that matched no record still returned rows on that server. An empty list therefore is not the only result of a call that replaced no address.

Source read on cPanel 11.138.0.24: with several domains and no sourceIp, the address is detected once, from whichever zone the server processes first, and reused for the others; that order is not the caller's. Pass sourceIp when the zones may hold different addresses. Temporary domains are skipped with a warning in responseMeta(); if all are skipped the result is an empty list.

Inspect the returned rows instead of treating envelope success as proof that an address changed. Zone changes for public domains are published and resolvers cache the old answers. The client makes one request with no readback, retry or rollback; a PayloadMismatchException after a successful envelope follows zones that already changed.
